body.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) be completed into confidence intervals for \((L,R)\) and a simultaneous confidence region for \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with asymptotic coverage uniform over regular branches, finite optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, and positive-dimensional stationary continua; and what is the exact directional limit on each singular stratum?
body.justification: Population sharpness does not by itself quantify sampling uncertainty at the branch switches that define the scientifically relevant frontier.
body.gap: Zhang--Tchetgen Tchetgen and Nabi et al. treat smooth sensitivity maps, while Fang--Santos gives generic directional theory; none handles this certified algebraic active-set geometry.
body.consumer: Empirical investigators need coverage statements for the entire set of confounding budgets that preserve a sign conclusion, including near ties.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform confidence regions across legal-root collisions and positive-dimensional stationary continua, together with the exact stochastic directional law on each such singular stratum, remain open.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen core specifies no sampling regularity, influence functions, nuisance-rate conditions, covariance nondegeneracy, or bootstrap coupling.  More importantly, at a root collision the active algebraic set itself changes with the observed-law direction, while at a stationary continuum its support functional can have a non-finite active index set.  The regular finite-branch delta calculation therefore does not imply uniform coverage over those strata.
obligation.attempted: Implicit differentiation closes unique nonsingular branches, and finite minima or maxima close finite regular ties.  Extending the same route to a colliding or positive-dimensional stationary set fails because neither a uniform metric expansion of the moving feasible correspondence nor an anti-concentration bound for the resulting Gaussian support functional is available from the stated primitives.
obligation.partial_result: On a regular branch with a unique optimizer and nonsingular stationary Jacobian, the implicit-function calculation used by \(\mathsf{CERT}\) makes \(L\) and \(R\) differentiable functions of the finite vector \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X}\).  At a finite tie of regular branches, the directional derivative of a minimum is the minimum of the tied branch derivatives, and the derivative of a maximum is their maximum.  These deterministic facts identify the candidate pointwise Gaussian directional limits once an asymptotically linear law for the observed-summary estimator is supplied.  They do not establish uniform validity near colliding roots or stationary continua.
